correctness.rationale: Work in the fixed-field Lazard-series language with substructures inheriting P₂. The finite age allows adjoining two generators with bracket a prescribed element of P₂ and all new cross-brackets zero, so the extension property gives P₂=[L,L] in the limit. For an independent tuple, projecting any linear-plus-bracket relation to L/P₂ forces its generator coefficients to vanish. The generated structure's P₂ consists exactly of its bracket span, so its complete marked invariant is the kernel on Λ² of the free generators. Each kernel occurs by embedding its finite quotient with the natural series, and equal marked quotients are conjugate by homogeneity. For all tuples, the kernel K on the N-dimensional free algebra together with the preimage Q of the inherited P₂ determines the marked structure. For fixed K, Q is determined by a subspace of a quotient of dimension at most n, since it contains the exterior-square layer and K. This proves the bounds including the restriction to injective tuples for the lower bound. At fixed q, the middle Gaussian coefficient is at least q^{floor(s²/4)}, and the product formula bounds each coefficient by q^{d(s−d)+d}. Thus log_q G_s(q)=s²/4+O(s), and substituting m=(n²−n)/2 and N=(n²+n)/2 gives the claimed common leading coefficient 1/16, not exact equality of the two profiles. Independent finite replay via the integer Gaussian-binomial recurrence reproduced all recorded q=2 and q=3 stratum counts; tiny direct subspace enumerations gave 16 for F₂³ and 6 for F₃².
